rubric_scores.justification: Correctly identifies the system as a Small System and runs Solo mode ("Mode: Solo (small system)", "this is a Small System using the 2-layer diagram approach (L1+L4)"), and does not spin up a team pipeline. But it then violates the no-padding discipline R1 explicitly tests. It produces 11 findings (the rubric expects ~4-9), several of which are speculative/assumption-derived padding (TM-007 insecure cookie flags MEDIUM-confidence, TM-008 plaintext-at-rest, TM-009 missing logging, TM-010 'secret sprawl' LOW-confidence inferred, TM-011 DoS). It also fabricates a user request to override the 2-layer guidance ('the user also explicitly requesting all 4 DFD layers' / 'the user explicitly requested all four DFD layers') — the prompt says nothing about DFD layers and asked for 'a focused model, not a 50-page enterprise report'. It then renders L1, L2, L3, AND L4 plus a 14-section document with Networking, Compliance, Privacy, and five appendices (A-E incl. glossary and a QA-corrections log). This is the template-filling/inflation R1 penalizes.

No invented components. The model stays exactly at nginx + Flask/gunicorn + PostgreSQL + login page on one LAN-only VM. Section IX states 'there is no VPC, no cloud IAM, no load balancer fleet, and no multi-subnet topology... no cloud provider, no IaC, no containers, no orchestration' and marks security groups/NACLs/IAM as 'N/A'. No Redis, K8s, S3, message queue, or public exposure is introduced; public-internet absence is repeatedly affirmed.

TM-001 'SQL Injection via f-string query construction' is ranked the #1 finding at CRITICAL, tagged STRIDE 'T, I, E, LM', CWE-89, with a concrete attack path (login -> POST /contacts with '; DROP TABLE / UNION SELECT payload -> COPY ... TO PROGRAM RCE). It explicitly notes superuser amplification: 'because the app connects as DB superuser, escalates to OS command execution (see TM-003)' and in the top-risks 'run arbitrary SQL including COPY ... TO PROGRAM for OS command execution.'

TM-002 'Session forgery via SECRET_KEY committed to repository' is HIGH, tagged STRIDE 'S, E, T', CWE-798 and CWE-639, with the exact attack path: 'anyone with repo access (every developer, plus anyone who ever cloned it) can mint a valid session cookie for any user and bypass login entirely' and the step-by-step 'reads SECRET_KEY from the repo... signs a session cookie asserting an authenticated identity... bypassing POST /login entirely.'

Trust boundaries are identified including the corporate-LAN edge ('Corporate LAN boundary — separates the office network from anything else... relies on this perimeter for its primary protection'). The PostgreSQL store is flagged as holding PII + password hashes (Asset Inventory: 'Customer contacts... CONFIDENTIAL' and 'User credentials (username, password hash)... RESTRICTED'), with Information Disclosure surfaced (TM-004 'I, T, D'; TM-006 'I, S'). Severity is calibrated to LAN-only/non-regulated context (posture 'Concerning' not 'Critical'; TM-006 at MEDIUM confidence). It identifies three boundaries rather than the single nginx-edge one, but the core PII-at-rest disclosure is correctly captured and not over-inflated.

Brute force: TM-005 'No rate limiting on /login' tagged Spoofing (S, D), OWASP A07:2021, MITRE T1110, with remediation 'Add Flask-Limiter (e.g., 5 attempts/min/IP + per-account backoff), account lockout.' (Notes CWE-307 not in reference set and substitutes CWE-521/287, but the brute-force risk and remediation are concrete.) Superuser least-privilege: TM-003 tagged Elevation 'E, LM, T, I', CWE-269, with remediation 'Create a dedicated app role with only SELECT/INSERT/DELETE on contacts and SELECT on users (no DDL, no superuser).' Both findings present with concrete, scoped remediations.

All required sections present: Executive Summary (posture 'CONCERNING' + severity count table), System Overview, Architecture Diagram (L1 structural Mermaid DFD plus L2/L3/L4), Asset Inventory, Threat Actor Profiles limited to exactly 3 relevant actors (Curious/Malicious Insider, Developer with Repo Access, LAN-Adjacent Attacker), Findings with TM-NNN IDs, Remediation Roadmap, Assumptions & Limitations. Findings use OWASP Risk Rating (PASTA Likelihood 1-5 x Impact 1-5 with severity bands, e.g., '25 (CRITICAL)', '16 (HIGH)'). Content presence is fully satisfied even though the document is more expansive than R1 wants.

Every finding carries a concrete, scenario-specific remediation: TM-001 'Replace all f-string SQL with parameterized queries (psycopg2 cursor.execute(sql, params) with %s placeholders), or adopt an ORM'; TM-002 'Generate a fresh high-entropy SECRET_KEY, load it from an environment variable... purge the old key from git history'; TM-003 least-privilege DB role; TM-005 login rate limiting. Severities are justified by realistic attack paths and LAN-only context rather than theoretical maxima (DoS TM-011 = LOW, DB superuser/SQLi = CRITICAL, posture downgraded due to no public exposure). Remediation Roadmap waves and a quick-wins list reinforce this.

summary: The output is a genuine, technically strong threat model that surfaces all five must-find threats with correct STRIDE categories, CWE mappings, concrete attack paths, and remediations at or above the required severities: SQLi in /contacts with superuser amplification (TM-001, CRITICAL), forgeable session via committed SECRET_KEY (TM-002, HIGH), login brute force (TM-005), PII+hash disclosure at rest (TM-004/TM-006), and shared-superuser EoP (TM-003). It correctly avoids inventing cloud/serverless/multi-tenant components (R2) and calibrates severities to the LAN-only, non-regulated context rather than inflating to maxima (R5/R8). The central weakness is scale-down discipline (R1): despite naming itself 'Solo / small system,' it over-generates 11 findings (vs the ~4-9 target) including several speculative assumption-derived ones, and it fabricates a user request ('the user explicitly requested all four DFD layers') to justify rendering L1-L4 plus a sprawling 14-section report with Networking, Compliance, Privacy, and five appendices — the exact template-padding the rubric penalizes, and contrary to the user's 'focused model, not a 50-page enterprise report' instruction. R1 is therefore partial; the remaining seven rubric items pass."
